highlights.title: Perplexity trusts GPT-6 Astra with end-to-end systems
highlights.summary: Perplexity uses Astra to write communications, change software, and monitor production systems, and checks in much less frequently than with earlier models.
body: As an AI-powered answer engine, Perplexity is deeply focused on search and accuracy. Its ability to process large amounts of information is critically important. Johnny Ho, Cofounder and Chief Strategy Officer, observes that every time the model gets better at writing code, Perplexity’s search engine improves too. It becomes able to write better programs that search the web and internal information and summarize it very concisely.
But the real challenge, according to Johnny, is taking those informational aspects and applying them to real-world systems. Something made easier with GPT‑6 Astra.
For Johnny, one of the most useful applications of AI is testing code. With limited time to test manually, he asks GPT‑6 Astra to build a small testing program around an application.

The model generates realistic responses like those another service would send, for example, a language model API or a connector. By standing in for those services, the model can check how the application responds and test the workflow from start to finish.

highlights.title: Awarding Man City's winner at Man Utd an error, admits refereeing body
highlights.summary: Refereeing body Pro Ref has admitted an error in awarding Manchester City's winner at Manchester United in their 1-0 victory at Old Trafford.
body: In a statement released just hours after Man City's win, Pro Ref revealed it had made contact with Man Utd to acknowledge an "error of judgment" and that the VAR "should have recommended an on-field review" for Erling Haaland's winner.
The striker's goal was initially disallowed for offside on the pitch before VAR overturned the decision.

The VAR officials deemed that Haaland was played onside by Man Utd defender Patrick Dorgu. However, Man City's Enzo Fernandez was in an offside position as he attempted to play the ball before it reached Haaland.

Despite not touching the ball, Fernandez's movement appeared to impact the defending of Man Utd's Lisandro Martinez before Haaland's back-post finish, which by the laws of the game should have led to the goal remaining disallowed.

highlights.title: World of Warcraft Forever Officially Brings Gamepad Controls Blizzard's MMO
highlights.summary: One of the biggest surprises from BlizzCon 2026 was Blizzard's reveal of World of Warcraft Forever, a new version of the long-running massively multiplayer online role-playing game that will give adventurers a new type of classic experience.
body: Blizzard had another World of Warcraft Forever surprise on the show floor: The MMO is playable on a gamepad, the first time that World of Warcraft has received such robust, official game controller support. Typically, the game is played with a keyboard and mouse — and a series of keybindings for spells and actions. We played World of Warcraft Forever ourselves with a gamepad, and it works surprisingly well.
But don't count on World of Warcraft Forever coming to consoles or handheld PCs any time soon. That's not really the goal of gamepad support in Forever, the game's developers tell Polygon.

"We’ve been thinking about World of Warcraft Forever as a third pillar of World of Warcraft," said Nora Valletta, lead software engineer on the game. "There's so much that we're delivering here, it felt like an opportunity for us to explore all manner of ideas, not just on gameplay front, but also how do players interface with our game?"

body: The US Open’s physical layout—at least within Arthur Ashe Stadium—looked slightly different this year. With tournament organizers adding some 2,000 seats to the arena’s lower bowl, Ashe’s suite levels were bumped up a floor and many were offered more real estate as a result. Ralph Lauren, the longtime outfitter of the tournament’s official apparel, made fantastic use of its new floor plan—turning its box into an ostensible remote and racquets-centric Polo Bar. Except, instead of the famed midtown Manhattan restaurant’s dark and cozy atmosphere, team RL went bright and brass-accented in Queens.
During finals weekend, Honey Deuces flowed and Coqodaq’s caviar-topped chicken nuggets arrived aplenty. Ralph Lauren even made custom packaging with the restaurant, solely for suite guests.

highlights.title: What’s behind the AI industry’s latest warnings of doom?
highlights.summary: On Equity, we discussed the AI industry's latest debate about whether it poses an existential threat to humanity.
body: The current discussion began after AI researcher Jacob Coxon said that he’s resigned from Anthropic because he’s worried that the leading AI companies are “gambling with our lives.” Then Anthropic’s alignment lead chimed in with a post declaring, “We really do earnestly believe AI could kill all humans!” adding that he personally thinks the chance is “>10% within the next decade.”

On the latest episode of TechCrunch’s Equity podcast, Kirsten Korosec, Sean O’Kane, and I discussed the latest apocalyptic warnings. I tried to articulate why I’m skeptical of many AI doomer narratives, while Kirsten asked if this was “just a weird way of flexing to show how far advanced their company’s AI model is,” particularly as these companies prepare to go public.

And Sean wondered how these concerns might show up in Anthropic’s S-1 filing for its IPO: “Are there junior lawyers right now who are going through and having to rewrite that entire section of the S-1 filing to say, ‘It’s a officially Anthropic’s position that there’s a more than 10% chance that we could develop something that would eradicate all of humanity and that would be materially bad for our business’?”

highlights.title: Blizzard Has No Plans To Turn Battle.net Into A Steam Competitor
highlights.summary: CD Projekt Red confirmed at BlizzCon that both The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt Remastered and Cyberpunk 2077 will come to Battle.net, Blizzard's proprietary game storefront, before the end of the year.
body: Battle.net predates Steam, having launched in 1997 alongside the original Diablo as a platform for player chats and listings of multiplayer servers. Over time, it became the hub for buying Blizzard (and only Blizzard) games on PC. Things stayed that way until Destiny 2 launched on the service in 2017. In the years since, other Activision-published series like Call of Duty and Crash Bandicoot made their way to Battle.net as well.

Following Microsoft's acquisition of Activision Blizzard, Xbox Game Studios and Bethesda titles like Avowed, Sea of Thieves, The Outer Worlds 2, and Doom: The Dark Ages also made their way to Battle.net. Now that CD Projekt Red games are coming to Battle.net, you'd be remiss not to wonder if we should expect a flood of other third-party titles to come in the future.
Despite this trend, Blizzard's Andrew Guerrero quickly made it clear during a BlizzCon interview with Polygon that Blizzard has no ambition of taking on the likes of Steam.

highlights.title: Obama urges Democrats to have a ‘clear plan’ for AI safeguards
highlights.summary: Obama recently said that Democrats need to make artificial intelligence one of their “central agendas” and “have a very clear plan” to address concerns around the technology’s economic impact and safety.
body: Obama made these comments on Thursday, at Democratic fundraising event where he was interviewed by House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries. The NYT says that Obama’s office provided a partial transcript of the event, at which Jeffries asked Obama how congressional Democrats should approach AI.
In response, Obama said that once Democrats regain the House majority, they need to “put together a framework for a very public conversation.”

“This is something that is moving very fast in private hands, and if we don’t get on top of it, I think can be dangerous,” Obama added. “If we do get on top of it, I do think it’s beneficial. I genuinely think it’s going to accelerate, for example, drug development in ways that can help us cure diseases.”

In a statement, Jeffries said the former president “is correct that decisive action must be taken on artificial intelligence.” Jeffries also said that “Republicans have abdicated their responsibility to govern on behalf of the American people.”

highlights.title: Norris calls for rule changes after 'unfair' Madrid defeat
highlights.summary: Lando Norris has called for a change to Formula 1's Virtual Safety Car rules after he lost out on victory to Kimi Antonelli at the Spanish Grand Prix.
body: Norris was six seconds ahead of Antonelli when a VSC (Virtual Safety Car) for Lance Stroll's stricken Aston Martin was called on Lap 15, which was a trigger point for everyone to make a pit stop as you lose less time by pitting under a VSC or Safety Car compared to normal green flag conditions.
However, Norris just passed the pit entry when the VSC came out, whereas his rivals behind could pit as they had not reached that part of the track.

The VSC only lasted two minutes, so Norris was unable to pit on the next lap as the VSC period ended just before he reached the pit entry. He pitted under green flag conditions and dropped to fifth on the track, before recovering to third by the end of the race.

"I was just unlucky. I was the only one on the whole grid to not get a pit stop and lost 20 seconds. This was out of there [the team's] control, my control. It's a rule that shouldn't define a race," Norris told Sky Sports F1.

highlights.title: 14 Years Later, TNT's Criminally Overlooked Action Series Is Officially Free on Streaming
highlights.summary: Looking back, the late 2000s marked a short, largely unsung golden age for quirky TV antiheroes. It was like every showrunner in Los Angeles tuned in to a marathon of The Saint around the same time, which led to a short but memorable fascination with crime-fighting criminals.
body: This was the heyday of shows about spies, thieves, and con men, who were all forced into using their skills to deal with worse crooks than themselves. For whatever reason, most of these ran on the USA Network, such as White Collar, Burn Notice, and Psych, but one of the best ran for five seasons on TNT.

That was Leverage, a weekly heist show about a crew of master criminals recruited for targeted scams against the rich and powerful. It's been a cult favorite for over a decade, but Leverage has also been notoriously hard to find in syndication or on streaming platforms. Now all but Leverage ’s most recent season has been made available for free on YouTube via ElectricNOW, the official channel of its production company Electric Entertainment.

Leverage begins with Nate Ford (Timothy Hutton), who used to be an insurance investigator. When Nate's own company refused to cover a treatment that could've saved his son's life, Nate quit the business.

highlights.title: ’60 Minutes’ Kicks Off Much-Scrutinized 59th Season With Old Ticks, Tricks
highlights.summary: CBS News says it needs to push “60 Minutes” into the future if the show is to survive, but the first telecast of the 59th season following a shocking overhaul of its on-air and behind-the-camera staff in May and June relied on many elements from the program’s past.
body: One of the stories even featured the old-time TV-news “hidden camera,” which many people thought went out of style after ABC News got sued in 1999 — and lost — for sending reporters to take footage at Food Lion supermarkets after lying on resumes and gaining access to tape unsanitary food practices. ABC News got tripped up on charges of trespassing and fraud, and hidden-camera reporting in the modern day is typically used mostly in public spaces or overseas, where U.S. laws don’t apply.

Will viewers miss Cecilia Vega, Sharyn Alfonsi, or Scott Pelley? The last of that trio, all pushed out of the show following the decision to oust top producers, was on nearly every week, often crashing a story tied to events that had taken place in the days leading up to broadcast.

Bari Weiss, the editor in chief of CBS News whose work at transforming the unit for modern audiences has stirred up a lot of controversy, wants “60 Minutes” to show up in more media venues and kick up livelier discussions. Other members of CBS News have felt this way as well, wondering if the program has gotten too soft or overly reliant on stories tied to the release of new books.

highlights.title: Unvaccinated Pennsylvania woman died of measles complications, coroner says
highlights.summary: A 40-year-old woman in Jefferson County, Pennsylvania has died of complications from measles, according to the county's coroner. It marks the third vaccine-preventable, measles-linked death in the US this year.
body: In a news release dated September 12, Jefferson County Coroner Greg Furlong said the death in the woman was “a heartbreaking loss for the family and an unfortunate reminder that measles can be a serious and potentially life-threatening disease.”
The county’s chief deputy coroner, Jason Stiver, added that “this tragedy highlights that measles should not be taken lightly.”

“Many people associate measles with a childhood illness, but it can lead to severe complications in individuals of any age,” Stiver said. “Measles is highly contagious and can result in serious respiratory illness, hospitalization, and in rare cases like this, death.”

While the news release stated that no additional information about the case would be provided, the New York Times obtained a preliminary death certificate. It indicated the woman had several chronic medical conditions, including chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), and she required supplemental oxygen at all times. Her health status made her vulnerable to complications from measles.

highlights.summary: Silicon Valley is shifting away from chatbot queries toward a future filled with resource-intensive agentic AI—and it's driving the data center buildout.
body: Welcome back to Power Play! Each week, senior writer Molly Taft tackles a topic around this midterm season’s biggest issue: data centers. If you’ve got a question or thought for the column, feel free to shoot Molly an email at [email protected] or reach them securely on Signal at mollytaft.76.
“What on earth are they building all of these data centers for? ” an exasperated friend asked me recently.

They’re not the only one asking: We got several similar questions on our recent data center livestream. It’s a really reasonable thing to wonder about. After all, if AI is already making all these breakthroughs, why are tech companies taking on billions of dollars of debt and constructing some of the biggest power plants in the world to build even more data centers?

highlights.title: JJ Watt proves to be a solid replacement for Tony Romo as CBS’s No 1 analyst
highlights.summary: With the former Dallas Cowboys quarterback on leave after his arrest in July, CBS brought a dependable presence into the booth with Jim Nantz. If you were looking for insight from the CBS team broadcasting Minnesota’s 39-22 comeback win over Green Bay on Sunday afternoon, you were rewarded even…
body: Asked by his play-by-play partner, Jim Nantz, what he was focusing on with new Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray, JJ Watt told viewers that Murray was playing against his former head coach Jonathan Gannon. The now-Green Bay defensive coordinator was dismissed from the head coaching job in Arizona at the end of last season.
“Let’s see what Gannon knows about Kyler and uses against him,” Watt told the audience.

“Jim, we wondered about the chess match between Gannon and Murray,” Watt said. “Gannon decided to send everybody in. Kyler Murray with a panic throw. He just chucked it up there! And it stayed in the air forever! Easy pick for Nixon. That’s a perfect example of Jonathan Gannon using some of his knowledge to get up in the face.”

It was a picture-perfect start for Watt, who never expected to be in the No 1 chair this season. But Watt’s situation changed after the arrest of Tony Romo in July, something that prompted CBS to place Romo on leave and move Watt up from the No 2 broadcasting team.

body: That's great news for Dragon Age fans, who will get another taste of Hepler's narrative work in 2029.

Hepler was previously a senior writer at BioWare, where she contributed heavily to the first three Dragon Age video games. In particular, Hepler really fleshed out the dwarven side of Thedas and many of Dragon Age 2 and Dragon Age: Inquisition 's most beloved characters. If you enjoy the writing and characters of the original Dragon Age trilogy, her involvement with Diablo 5 makes the game's narrative potential much more interesting.

While Dragon Age 2 is fondly remembered nowadays, at the time of the game's release, players did not take kindly to the sequel's reduced scope and issues with the combat. Shortly after Dragon Age 2's release, comments made by Hepler years prior about combat in video games were weaponized by online provocateurs, who tried to pin Dragon Age 2's biggest flaws on Hepler's involvement.

highlights.title: Cynthia Erivo’s Riveting ‘Prima Facie’ Performance Earns TIFF Standing Ovation
highlights.summary: Cynthia Erivo already earned two best actress Oscar nominations for portraying Harriet Tubman and the green-skinned Elphaba in “Wicked” — not to mention her Tony-winning work in “The Color Purple” — but her latest film, “Prima Facie,” might be her most challenging high-wire act yet.
body: White (“Bleak House,” “Jane Eyre,” “Woman Walks Ahead”) directed the adaptation by playwright Suzie Miller from her globally acclaimed one-woman show. The film is one of the hottest sales titles on the block at TIFF. Jodie Comer won the Tony and Olivier awards for the stage version, and Erivo proved equally captivating on the big screen — albeit under a the very racial and socioeconomic context. Erivo’s Tessa is a woman of color from a working class background, navigating a system bolstered by white men dating back to medieval times in the London court.

“We got the chance to meet a lot of Black women barristers. I understood that they sort of work in a different rhythm to everybody else, and the way they approach court is very much making it their own,” Erivo said at a Q&A following the premiere “I wanted that for Tessa, I wanted her to have this outside life that influenced the way she approached [her work].”

body: The Republicans fear slowing down AI development could give China the edge.

Donald Trump and House Speaker Mike Johnson, however, seem to think the AI executives are being overreactive and fear that a pause could lead to China outpacing the US in the AI race. According to the Financial Times, Trump said “Look, we’re leading China in AI... and, frankly, I want to keep it that way, because whoever wins AI, wins.”

Johnson echoed those sentiments on CNN, telling Jake Tapper that rushing to place restrictions on AI development could be a “national security threat.” He urged people not to panic. “If Congress just races in and does some sort of emergency session to try and regulate AI, we will lose the race to China.”

highlights.title: OpenAI’s rogue AI tried to hack another company in May
highlights.summary: In May, hundreds of malicious and spam packages were uploaded to RubyGems, causing a serious disruption for the host. Now independent researchers have said that a swarm of OpenAI agents were responsible for the attack. Not only that, but the AI tried to steal users' API keys.
body: The previously undisclosed attack on Ruby Gems predates Hugging Face by more than a month.

The agents in this instance managed to bypass RubyGems’ email verification system to create a large number of accounts, then overwhelmed it with submissions. It then used the site’s automatic build system to remotely execute code and tried to exploit a vulnerability to steal user API keys. Though, it’s unclear if it ever succeeded.

OpenAI disputed the findings. Spokesperson Kayla Wood told The Verge that, “Based on our review, our agents used the RubyGems platform to access the internet to carry out benign tasks and retrieve public information. We’ll continue to investigate as part of our broader review of agent activity during training and evaluation.”

highlights.title: Not glamorous, but common: how to manage dandruff at home and when to get help
highlights.summary: Experts don’t know exactly what causes dandruff, but if you’re seeing light flakes on your scalp, over-the-counter products can help. You spy a scatter of white flakes on your collar. Or you’ve got an itch that won’t quit, no matter how much you wash your hair.
body: An itchy, flaking scalp is rarely dangerous, but it can be annoying. Here’s what you need to know about what might be causing your flakes, what you can do about it, and when it’s time to get help.

Dandruff is the mildest form of a condition called seborrheic dermatitis, a type of skin inflammation that usually affects the head, face or trunk. At its worst, this condition leads to patches of red skin covered in tiny, greasy scales. However, most people with dandruff have just minor scaliness and no redness, affecting only the scalp.

Experts still don’t know exactly what causes dandruff, and it’s likely there are various contributing factors. A yeast called Malassezia is a leading suspect, says James Pathoulas, an assistant professor of dermatology at the University of Minnesota medical school who specializes in hair and scalp disorders. Malassezia usually lives harmlessly on the scalp, but overgrowth has been linked with scalp inflammation.

highlights.title: ‘Prima Facie’ Review: Cynthia Erivo Stars as a Lawyer Who Becomes a Rape Victim in This Misfire of an Adaptation
highlights.summary: The Oscar nominee tackles the role originated by Jodie Comer on the West End and Broadway in Susanna White's film version of Suzie Miller's award-winning play.
body: Directed by Susanna White, whose smart works include the series Generation Kill and the thriller Our Kind of Traitor, the film opens with some of its heaviest-handed imagery. As Tessa bounces up the steps of the Old Bailey courthouse, already wearing her robe and white courtroom wig, the camera focuses on her out-of-place black-sequined sneakers. She steps into a room full of sleek, posh-looking women lawyers and in the first of her voiceovers, many taken directly from the play, says, “Thoroughbreds, that’s how I see them.” The film then cuts to images of — really, it’s this literal — horses.

Before long she has sex in the office with another rising-star lawyer, the privileged Julian. “I want this,” her unnecessary voiceover says. Julian is played with winning charm by Daniel Ings in a role that stretches him from his usual parts, like the buffoonish screw-up brother in the series The Gentlemen. Casting is not one of this film’s problems.
points: The Oscar nominee tackles the role originated by Jodie Comer on the West End and Broadway in Susanna White's film version of Suzie Miller's award-winning play.

highlights.title: Always Read the Care Label! Inside Poshmark’s Dry Cleaner Party During NYFW
highlights.summary: Elizabeth von der Goltz, Poshmark’s Chief Revenue Officer, hosted a downtown preview of the platform’s now-open-to-the-public NYFW activation, which also marks the launch of the new Try Yourself On brand campaign.
body: Upon arrival, guests were welcomed into a replica of a classic dry cleaner—complete with a working garment conveyor. Out back, a speakeasy-style cocktail lounge and showroom awaited. The idea for the set-up, which echoes the campaign imagery, came from people’s tendency to bring only their most rare and treasured items to be professionally cleaned.

In this spirit, ambassadors from the new Tastemakers campaign—think: Chloe Fineman, Courtney Grow, Colleen Allen, Jalil Johnson, Elissa Santisi and her daughter Francesca Keller—had lent pieces from their personal wardrobes to create a special NYFW collection. (You can also now follow them and shop their pre-loved pieces in the app.) Crowd favorites included a pair of feather-trimmed Prada mules, a beaded Phoebe Philo-era Chloé bag, and a Roberto Cavalli Spring 2003 mini dress that was—much to everyone’s disappointment—not for sale.
